section_1.title: Introduction: The Guessing Game Challenge
section_1.content: Define Wordle as a search problem in a finite state space of 2,315 possible answers. Introduce the goal: minimizing the average number of guesses using information theory.
section_1.example: Imagine a detective (The Solver) trying to identify a secret animal code out of 2,315 candidates. Each guess is an interrogation.

section_2.title: Mathematical Foundation: Entropy as Information Gain
section_2.content: Explain that every guess provides feedback (Green/Yellow/Gray). Prerequisite: Define Entropy H(X) = -Σ p(x)log2 p(x). Visually represent this as a decision tree branch splitting probabilities.
section_2.example: A guess like 'CRANE' acts as a filter: it partitions the 2,315 words into subsets based on possible color patterns, aiming to maximize the 'expected surprise'.

section_3.title: Algorithmic Analysis: Greedy Search vs. Optimal Path
section_3.content: Contrast a 'Greedy' strategy (picking the most likely remaining word) with the 'Max Entropy' strategy (picking the word that reduces the remaining search space most efficiently).
section_3.example: Compare a robot choosing a word that eliminates 90% of candidates versus one that only eliminates 10%, visualizing the narrowing search area on a screen.

section_4.title: Practical Application: Why 'CRANE' or 'SALET'?
section_4.content: Analyze why specific starting words are mathematically superior. They maximize vowel frequency and common consonant positioning, providing the highest average information gain per turn.
section_4.example: Visual overlay of a heat map showing character frequency across the 2,315-word dictionary, highlighting why 'S', 'A', 'R', 'E' are the 'Golden Keys'.

section_5.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_5.content: Recap: Optimal play is not about guessing the word immediately; it is about maximizing the information gained in the first two turns to collapse the uncertainty of the system.
section_5.example: Final screen: An animation showing a 'cloud of possibilities' shrinking rapidly from 2,315 to 1, then 0, after an optimal 'CRANE' start.
